• S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”

• Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 13 (13 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 13 Nov 2026, version re-checked 14 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

• S5-R10b: “The as-of date can be any day, including a day after today, as today. For a day after today the report counts everything entered so far and counts days past due to the picked day; the chip, the PDF and the CSV all show the picked day. A link with an as-of date opens on that date.”

• S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”

• S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. There are no page buttons. A/R Detail and A/P Detail show each bucket's first 100 lines, then load more as the user scrolls (S4-R4). Paging never repeats or skips a customer, vendor or row, in any sort. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices, an open customer or vendor shows its first 100 documents, then the next 100 as the user scrolls; its document count, its subtotals, the Totals row and the exports always cover all of its documents. The documents of an open customer or vendor may all arrive from the server in one request; this rule sets only how many are shown at a time.”
